clap.context: Two hands clapping. Used for applause and praise reactions, congratulations messages, well-done badges and audience feedback.

fist-bump.context: Two fists bumping knuckles. Used for teamwork and friendly greetings, respect or agreement reactions, deal-done moments and community apps.

hand-call-me.context: A hand with the thumb and little finger stretched out, the call me or shaka sign. Used for call-me buttons and phone contact, hang loose or surf themes, and friendly greetings.

hand-click.context: A pointing finger with small click marks around its tip. Used for click here prompts, link and button hints in tutorials, pointer cursors and click-through stats.

hand-coins.context: An open hand holding coins. Payments and payouts, earnings and salary, tips and donations, and cashback or refund screens use it.

hand-crossed-fingers.context: A hand with the index and middle fingers crossed, for good luck. Used for wishes and hopes, waiting on results, promises and luck-themed reactions.

hand-grab.context: A hand gripping a bar. Used for grab and drag handles, grip or hold actions, move tools, and grab rails on transit and accessibility signs.

hand-heart.context: An open hand holding up a heart. Used for charity and donations, care and kindness, volunteering, health care services and customer care pages.

hand-ok.context: A hand making the OK sign, thumb and index finger forming a ring. Used for approval and okay reactions, all-good status, agreement and quality checks.

hand-peace.context: A hand making a V sign with two fingers raised. Used for peace and victory, the number two, friendly goodbyes and photo poses, and win states in games.

hand-pinch.context: A thumb and index finger pinching something small. Used for pinch-to-zoom hints in onboarding, touch gesture guides, a pinch in recipes and fine adjustments.

hand-point-down.context: A hand pointing down with its index finger. Used for see below prompts, scroll down hints, next-section cues and pointing at content underneath.

hand-point-left.context: A hand pointing left with its index finger. Used for back and previous actions, pointing at content on the left, direction hints and swipe-left cues.

hand-point-right.context: A hand pointing right with its index finger. Used for next and continue actions, pointing at content on the right, step-by-step guides and call-to-action hints.

hand-point-up.context: A hand pointing up with its index finger. Used for see above prompts, back to top and scroll up hints, raising a point or question, and the number one.

hand-rock.context: A hand making the horns sign, index and little fingers raised. Rock music and concerts, gigs and festivals, rock on reactions and party themes use it.

hand-shake-deal.context: Two hands clasped in a handshake under small burst marks, a deal sealed. Used for agreements and contracts, partnerships, closed sales and successful negotiations.

hand-stop.context: A raised flat palm with the fingers held together. Used for stop and halt, blocking or declining, wait and no entry signs, and messages about boundaries.

hand-swipe.context: A finger swiping sideways. Common in swipe gestures in onboarding, carousels, slide-to-unlock hints and touch tutorials.

hand-tap.context: A finger tapping, with ripples around its tip. Used for tap here prompts, touch gesture guides, contactless or tap-to-pay hints and button presses on mobile.

hand-wave.context: A tilted open hand with motion marks, waving. Used for hello and welcome messages, goodbye screens, greetings in chat and onboarding intros.

hand-write.context: A hand writing with a pen. Used for signatures and e-signing, writing or editing notes, handwriting input, forms to fill in and journaling.

pray.context: Two palms pressed together. Used for please and thank you, prayer and gratitude, namaste greetings, hoping for something and respectful apologies.

thumbs-down.context: A thumbs-down hand. Used for dislikes and downvotes, negative feedback, rejecting or disapproving, not helpful buttons and poor ratings.

thumbs-up.context: A thumbs-up hand. Used for like buttons and upvotes, positive feedback, was this helpful prompts, and approval or okay replies.
